columnRef.help: The measured column, label Values Column: a numeric column with the values in time order. The chart is computed from 5 numbers on, all of which must be greater than 0 (Box-Cox); empty and non-numeric cells are skipped, text such as “2,5” as well. With fewer numbers the output stays empty, a value less than or equal to 0 gives an error message. Empty until one is chosen; an empty value clears the choice. A change recomputes.

lambdaMode.help: How the λ of the Box-Cox transformation is obtained, label λ mode: 'auto' (auto (Anderson-Darling)) estimates it from the data, 'manual' takes lambdaManual. The estimate picks, from a grid from −3 to 3 in steps of 0.05, the λ at which the transformed values have the smallest Anderson-Darling statistic (closest to a normal distribution), rounded to 0.01. Any other value is rejected. instance.set only switches the mode; the mode-switch command also adopts a λ when switching to 'manual', just as the selection in the interface adopts the estimated λ. A change recomputes.

lambdaManual.help: The λ of the Box-Cox transformation y = (x^λ − 1)/λ in 'manual' mode, label λ; for |λ| < 10⁻⁸ the log transformation y = ln x applies. Any finite number, default 0. It only takes effect in 'manual' mode; in 'auto' mode the stored value stays as it is and recomputes nothing, the field is disabled and shows the estimated λ (asyncTasks.analysis.value.result.lambda). When switching to 'manual', the mode-switch command adopts the estimated λ as the starting value.

chart.help: The settings from the chart editor of the control chart (title, axis titles, font sizes, background, reference lines, point color, symbol, size and outline of the series); empty as long as nothing was changed.

exampleWorksheetId.help: The id of the example worksheet this module was loaded from; empty if it does not come from an example.

activeParams.help: The parameter fields instance.set currently writes with effect: lambdaMode, and lambdaManual in 'manual' mode.

activeColumnSlots.help: The column fields instance.set currently writes with effect: columnRef.

setLambdaMode.help: Switches how λ is obtained, in one step. When switching to 'manual', a given λ is adopted into lambdaManual (the interface passes the estimated λ of the last result); without λ, lambdaManual stays as it is. When switching to 'auto', lambdaManual is left unchanged.

params.mode: The new way: 'auto' or 'manual'. Any other value is an error.
params.lambda: Optional: the λ adopted into lambdaManual when switching to 'manual', a finite number or null. No effect in 'auto' mode.
params.command: The command as one object with mode and optionally lambda.

analysis.help: Computes the transformed individuals chart from the measured column and the λ mode; runs by itself after every change of the column, the λ mode or, in 'manual' mode, lambdaManual and after changes in the worksheet (batched, 120 ms delay). The value is { result, points, error, message }: result is the result (each figure described individually under keys), points one row { transformed, signal } per usable number in data order. Without a column, with a deleted column or with fewer than 5 numbers result is null, points is empty and error is null. If a value is less than or equal to 0, error gives the reason 'errPositiveOnly'; if the computation fails (also with non-finite transformed values or limits), 'errCompute'. message is then the text of the error message in the language of the interface, otherwise null.

Result.n: Number of usable numbers in the series; empty and non-numeric cells are already removed. A result exists from 5 numbers on, all of which must be greater than 0. The numbers of the signal points count these numbers from 0, not the worksheet rows.
Result.lambda: The λ used for the Box-Cox transformation y = (x^λ − 1)/λ; for |λ| < 10⁻⁸ it is the log transformation y = ln x. In “auto” mode it is the estimated λ (smallest Anderson-Darling statistic on the grid from −3 to 3, step 0.05, rounded to 0.01), in “manual” mode the entered one. The tile shows it with three decimals and the suffix (auto) or (manual).
Result.lambdaAuto: Whether λ was estimated from the data (true) or set by hand (false). The tile shows it as the suffix (auto) or (manual) after λ.
Result.i: The individuals chart on the transformed scale y: center line, upper and lower control limit and spread σ̂. These are the values of the “transformed (y)” column in the table.
Result.iOriginal: The same limits of the individuals chart, converted back to the original scale: x = (λ·y + 1)^(1/λ), for the log transformation x = e^y. They are not symmetric around the center line. A value is missing (empty, “–” in the table) when λ·y + 1 ≤ 0, so the back-transformation is undefined there; typically that hits the lower limit for λ > 0.
Result.mr: The moving range chart of the transformed values: center line MR̄ (mean of the absolute differences |yᵢ − yᵢ₋₁| of consecutive values), upper control limit 3.267 · MR̄, lower 0. It exists on the transformed scale only.
Result.signals: Numbers (counted from 0 among the usable numbers) of the points whose transformed value lies above the UCL or below the LCL of the individuals chart. The “Signals” tile shows their count.

IndividualLimits.cl: Center line of the individuals chart on the transformed scale: the mean ȳ of all transformed values (tile CL (y)). The tile's sub-line shows the spread σ̂.
IndividualLimits.ucl: Upper control limit (UCL) of the individuals chart on the transformed scale: center line + 3 · σ̂.
IndividualLimits.lcl: Lower control limit (LCL) of the individuals chart on the transformed scale: center line − 3 · σ̂.
IndividualLimits.sigma: Estimated spread σ̂ of the transformed values: MR̄/1.128, with the mean MR̄ of the moving ranges and the factor d₂ = 1.128 for pairs. The sub-line of the CL (y) tile shows it.

Limits.ucl: Upper control limit (UCL) of the chart.
Limits.lcl: Lower control limit (LCL) of the chart.

Point.transformed: The transformed value y of a usable number, in the order of the column; this is what is plotted.
Point.signal: True when the transformed value lies above the UCL or below the LCL of the individuals chart.
